scope: Analyst review of question and options only; not video-grounded annotations or coverage gold. All three datasets inform algorithm design.

needs: subject translation in initial body frame
cases.finding: One option conjoins translation and turning. Resolve whether turning denotes heading of the path or body rotation before choosing its observable.
Moving-camera version should use the same task recipe and different evidence reliability; it should not be a benchmark-specific kind.
Orbit needs a defined centre or a documented path convention. Sideways translation plus opposing pan is not sufficient.
A dominant pan label discards the forward/backward distinction required by every option.
Existing scalar range is appropriate. Unreliable geometry should support unknown, not a fabricated trend.
Bearing depends on both parties and the frame anchor; it is not the same quantity as subject heading change.
Distance cannot distinguish the referee's left/right. Even a new image-relative-position tool would not resolve the stated body frame.
Options require lateral and depth components together, not just one nearest axis.
Existing whole-window rhythm/shake labels cannot directly rank four option-defined windows.
Phase percentages and literal timestamps are not perfectly consistent. Preserve the ambiguity and explicit intervals instead of silently collapsing the options.
A single group centroid cannot distinguish a static cluster from people rotating around a fixed centre.
Options require complementary measurements; no single scalar pair_relation label covers them.
Nearest-surface distance cannot distinguish walking along a path from crossing it. Backward walking adds a body-facing requirement.
The original predicates must survive decomposition; mapping both to other destroys the question.
Question stem supplies no event nouns. A two-event, question-noun-only slot schema cannot represent the alternatives.
Visibility gaps need intervals and identity continuity, not only first and last presence.
Number of annotated tracked objects is not generally identifiable from RGB. Keep this separate from visual instance count; do not expose GT masks.
Subject-relative orbit must be measured around the named subject; camera pan alone is insufficient.
Existence is a prerequisite shared with motion, not merely another motion label. A failed segmentation is not proof of absence.
Filtered instance count composes a set with a predicate. Counting all people answers a different question.
Negated predicates need an unknown state: no reliable motion track does not imply not moving.

needs: ball direction conditional on each hit
cases.finding: Count ball-hit events, not bat motion cycles, balls, or people.
Anatomical left/right is not image left/right; localize the action before assigning the hand.
The event count must be conditioned on actor and hand. Generic periodicity alone is insufficient.
This counts encountered trees, not generic repeated motion. Keep entity identity attached to each event.
Spoons here are event/portion units; a SAM instance count of spoon objects is semantically wrong.
Projected spin, body yaw and orbit around a point are distinct. Resolve the intended motion before reusing orientation.
A spinning wheel can have a stationary centre and no unique semantic front. Translation and OAV front-facing are insufficient.
Counting, relations and grounding should compose rather than multiply families for each combination.
This is a relational state transition, not a static hand label.
Relative speed can be measured in common scene units without metric calibration. Head-camera pose is not automatically torso motion.
The first event establishes a reference for a later spatial question. Requires event localization composed with a relation.
